title: A prescribed residue-field basis of a finitely presented module spreads to a basis
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, and $M$ a finitely presented $A$-module (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus u}\to A^{\oplus v}\to M\to0$ for some $u,v\ge0$). Let $m_1,\dots,m_r\in M$ be elements whose images form a basis of the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-vector space $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and suppose $M_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module of rank $r$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there is $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that the images $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$ form a basis of the localized $A_f$-module $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free): lift the chosen basis to a map from a finite free module and use Lemma Tag 05GF (lemma-map-between-finitely-presented) and Lemma Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local) to make that map an isomorphism after localization; this statement keeps the prescribed lifts
